expectation: A standalone chat left in the store as a hidden board task is converted once into its own model: it keeps its ID so the existing conversation transcript stays attached, keeps its provider session, carries its in-flight turn state across with the status message and progress report that explain it, is removed from the board so it never lists or resolves as a task, and reopening the chat returns that same migrated chat rather than creating a second one.

Each standalone chat page is its own provider session: the first turn of a page starts a fresh session carrying the system prompt plus only that page's own turns, later turns on that page resume it without repeating the page context, and a different page never shares it, so an earlier page's turns never reach a later page. An annotation that quotes an earlier page carries just that page into the current turn, and rotating sessions still leaves every page's messages visible in the transcript.

The Chat button opens the standalone chat — its own model rather than a board task — in a sliding sidebar that never appears on the board, task commands cannot reach it by ID, and the bridge rejects any attempt to add a repository or worktree root to it. The GUI composer works without a configured repository parent and omits task status, repository controls, the Changes sidebar, and the no-repository-selected banner. Its CLI page close-turn signal keeps a continuing reply on the active page and starts a new titled page on a topic change, a completed turn's user and assistant messages persist onto the active page without leaking onto other pages, and pages are findable by search. Each page is also stored in a separate atomic JSON file in a discoverable archive directory; pages already present before file archiving are backfilled once, and each file tracks current metadata and messages. A turn that omits close-turn is tracked as missed, then a background low-effort Luna fallback rejects one malformed classification and retries, moves both messages to its correctly titled page, keeps page evaluation visually quiet while the primary answer remains usable, then updates the transcript separator with the title when classification completes; a following send waits for that decision, and preserves chronological order on a later append. An explicit page start during a pending fallback cancels its stale result, keeps the missed turn on its original page, and clears the warning. If all helper results are invalid, the pending decision remains durable, blocks the next provider send, and retries after the helper recovers; the UI keeps the unresolved state visually quiet and sends successfully once recovery completes. Earlier pages stay visible in the transcript after their page session rotates, and a board task conversation rejects a chat page as turn context. While a chat turn is held active, queuing a follow-up on the chat resolves the chat rather than a board task and the queued message can be removed, and selecting the provider the chat already uses returns the chat unchanged instead of failing. The chat's own turn state changes (In Progress, then Waiting Response) during a send, and it never renders as a card on the visible Kanban board in any state. A chat turn that ran close-turn gets no nudge, and a Codex chat turn that skipped it gets exactly one nudge through the shared recovery loop, asking for close-turn on its reply and never for a task outcome, because the chat has no board status; its developer instructions teach it that task language means Playhouse's own board and give it the Playhouse task CLI, and they never ask it to write the page title into its visible answer. Opening a board task while the chat sidebar is showing replaces it with that task's conversation view instead of showing both at once, and returning to the board reveals the chat sidebar again, with the chat's own model left untouched by the unrelated task. The visible chat panel opens at full board-content height, overlaps the logo header and narrow board sidebar, and hides the covered branding and sidebar controls from accessibility navigation while open; it raises the board's minimum width by the chat panel width, so the window grows to keep the shifted columns visible; it pushes the columns to the panel’s right edge; closing chat reveals the sidebar and moves the columns back beside it while the window keeps its grown width. Dragging the chat sidebar's right border resizes it, between a 320-point minimum and the larger of its default width and the screen width the board's minimum width leaves free, and reopening the sidebar, even after an app relaunch, keeps the dragged width. The border's grab strip extends only out over the board, never over the transcript's scroller along its inner side, so pressing and dragging just inside the border leaves the width unchanged. While the edge moves, the chat keeps the width it was last laid out at, clipped to the panel, and its transcript reflows to the panel's width when the drag ends.

When a standalone chat uses Claude, a missed page signal invokes the Haiku helper at low effort; a malformed result is rejected and retried, an unrelated later question and its assistant reply move to a new titled page, the UI keeps page evaluation visually quiet without blocking the primary answer, updates the transcript separator when classification completes, and holds a following send until the decision resolves, and appends the related follow-up in chronological order. The Claude-specific model and effort arguments are verified through the real CLI/XPC path. An explicit page start during a pending fallback cancels its stale result, keeps the missed turn on its original page, and clears the warning. If all helper results are invalid, the pending decision remains durable, blocks the next provider send, and retries after the helper recovers; the UI keeps the unresolved state visually quiet and sends successfully once recovery completes.

Clicking Stop during Codex reasoning immediately moves the task to Waiting Response and sends Codex's turn-scoped turn/interrupt request. The accepted interruption settles the send without changing the task to Blocked, and a fresh CLI/XPC read confirms the status persisted. A fresh `conversation runtime` read from the daemon reports the turn active and interruptible while it thinks, and interrupted but no longer active once the stop settles. The turn's activity section renders open for as long as the daemon reports the turn active, and folds once the stop settles with no final answer.

Clicking Stop during Claude reasoning immediately moves the task to Waiting Response and sends Claude's session-scoped control interrupt. The accepted interruption settles the send without changing the task to Blocked, and a fresh CLI/XPC read confirms the status persisted. A fresh `conversation runtime` read from the daemon reports the turn active and interruptible while it thinks, and interrupted but no longer active once the stop settles. The turn's activity section renders open for as long as the daemon reports the turn active, and folds once the stop settles with no final answer.

If Codex rejects turn/interrupt while its turn is still active, Stop reports the provider failure and the task returns to In Progress; releasing the fixture lets the original turn complete normally into Waiting Response.

If Claude rejects its session control interrupt while its turn is still active, Stop reports the provider failure and the task returns to In Progress; releasing the fixture lets the original turn complete normally into Waiting Response.

Playhouse opens one main board window titled with its worktree label, displays the transparent theater logo in the board header, keeps a fixed standard-width (200-point) Kanban sidebar and left of the columns while they scroll, and places its Scheduled Tasks button inside the sidebar below the full logo header. The Dock AppIcon uses the same foreground artwork on a solid #2C2F36 background, and the bridge reports API version 1.

The primary and linked source worktrees resolve to stable, distinct app and XPC identities, build paths, data stores, logs, and managed worktree roots, each worktree root inside its data directory. The run.sh launch resolver replaces a PLAYHOUSE_DATA_DIRECTORY inherited from another Playhouse app's profile directory with the launching worktree's own and rejects any other foreign data directory, and run.sh drops PLAYHOUSE_BRIDGE_SERVICE_NAME and PLAYHOUSE_BRIDGE_SOCKET_PATH inherited from another Playhouse app, saying so, while keeping the launching worktree's own bridge. After its build and right before it opens the app, run.sh again stops this worktree's app and bridge daemon, so a daemon started from the previous build during the build cannot serve the new app. A saved conversation remains visible after an app restart.

New Task opens with the repository picker closed and composer focused; no selected repository is valid and shows no red missing-folder warning when the required repository root is configured. A standalone conversation can be sent without repository roots, while GUI and CLI reject sends if the configured repository root is missing. The UI and CLI accept standalone sends after the root is configured. The CLI accepts empty-root tasks and rejects blank titles, missing folders, unavailable roots, and invalid merge targets.

A directly created conversation can add repositories in order, edit pending branch settings, and add a context folder; these settings persist across fresh connections without creating branches or worktrees before the first send. The conversation shows the additional context folder without repeating repository worktrees in a Working in summary. Saving an unsent prompt records task creation, prompt save, and subsequent reads with safe argument metadata, result state, and outcome while excluding prompt text.
A selected existing branch remains pending until task start, then reuses its exact existing worktree path.

The conversation picker can add multiple repositories; unset branch settings display defaults and persist pending auto records resolved to local main without creating branches or worktrees before the first send.
A folder-only task persists its context without Git worktrees and reaches Done after a successful turn without attempting a merge.
Adding a repository branch already assigned to another active task is rejected in the new conversation, and the existing task and repository reservation remain unchanged.
Two concurrent CLI/XPC creates targeting the same explicit branch in one repository serialize through a shared cross-process lock, leaving exactly one persisted active task and rejecting the other.

If another process holds the shared task-store write lock when a Codex turn completes after an explicit completed outcome, final status persistence waits and then saves Review status and full history across fresh CLI/XPC reads. Correlated persistence diagnostics include task ID, store path, lock wait, attempts, and retry count; task reads correlate started and completed events by read ID and store path, while failed reads include store file and sidecar state. Reopening the conversation in the UI shows the saved exchange without a store error.

A real ModelContainer open failure against an isolated invalid store path returns an error and durably logs the phase, exact underlying NSError domain/code/userInfo, resolved store path, file/sidecar snapshot, and read-only schema probe failure; the paired visible UI case keeps Playhouse open on its normal board while the same isolated CLI/XPC request fails and verifies the persisted diagnostic.

A real SwiftData fetch failure against an isolated store with a missing task column returns an error and logs a correlated read ID, NSError domain/code/userInfo, store path, file/sidecar snapshot, and the exact missing-column message from a read-only schema probe before the CLI/XPC request completes; the paired visible UI case keeps the normal task board open and verifies the same isolated failure record.

A real legacy SwiftData task store with in-progress timing columns and no submitted-prompt column waits for the store-write lock while CLI/XPC reads concurrently; migration backs up before adding the missing VARCHAR prompt column as nullable with no default and preserves elapsed time at zero. The CLI preserves the task and its saved prompt, which a store from before drafts were flagged does not restore as a draft, and the visible app opens the migrated store with an empty composer that keeps the saved prompt through a subsequent restart with duration still zero; metadata advances and later opens create no additional backup. The store is imported once into the protected filename and the legacy database remains unchanged. Committed WAL-only saved prompt data survives import, and a subsequent edited draft survives restart without reimport.

A test-built Playhouse service rejects a data directory outside the temporary test area and a linked store inside it before creating or opening either store; the visible app remains on its isolated board and can still read its tasks.

Tasks with the same automatic branch choice remain pending without creating a worktree before conversation start. When one task has claimed the generated branch, a send from the other (through the CLI) succeeds with its own suffixed branch and a separate worktree, leaving both tasks started; the opt-in live provider integration sends both turns concurrently and confirms each task gets a distinct branch and worktree.

Sending the first message derives an auto branch from the generated task title, with a prompt fallback when title generation fails. Every linked PR must be merged before the task can move to Done. App focus checks each linked PR no more than once per 20 seconds; rapid focus changes are coalesced into one refresh after the cooldown. An unmerged PR keeps its link and suppresses the completion button. PR links and the green completion button have hit targets of at least 30×30 points. After all PRs merge, a later focus check replaces their links with a green completion button; clicking it waits for the task lock and then trusts that already-confirmed merge state, moving the task to Done immediately without re-querying GitHub even if merge status changed while the lock was held. The CLI's task move command has no such cached state, so it always verifies merge status directly with GitHub before completing, including rechecking after waiting for a contended task lock, and reports unmerged pull requests instead of completing when a PR is not actually merged. Completion removes managed worktrees while preserving their branches, does not merge into the local target, retains conversation history, and exposes the task in the searchable archive, whose conversation keeps its composer for follow-up questions; the CLI searches matching local Codex JSONL session files, including current input_text and output_text message content, without loading conversation histories, while the visible archive searches both user input_text and assistant output_text, loads the newest 40 first, and reveals older tasks as the user scrolls. While only some linked PRs are merged, each merged PR's number shows in merged purple and the task offers no completion checkmark until all are merged.

Two tasks with the same title and an automatic branch on one repository both start: the first gets the title slug, the second a fresh branch named like the slug plus a hyphen and four lowercase letters or digits, in a different worktree. An existing local branch named like the slug, with no task using it, is never checked out: a new automatic task gets a suffixed fresh branch started from its branch-from. The visible task conversation shows the resolved suffixed branch.

Moving a reviewed task to Done removes its managed worktree and keeps its branch and target commit without committing or merging. When the worktree holds uncommitted changes the move is refused until the user confirms discarding them: declining keeps the task in Review with its files intact, and confirming removes them. A reviewed task stays in Review until it is moved; in the UI the Done drawer rests as a thin sliver beside, not over, the board columns, opens only while a reviewed card is dragged, and returns to rest both after a card is dropped on Done and when a card is dropped back in place without moving the task.

A Done task keeps its conversation open: the UI shows the composer with an archived hint naming the merge target instead of a read-only notice, and its changes read reports no changes rather than a Git error for the removed worktree; and a follow-up sent from a Done task runs a real provider turn in the source repository of its removed worktree. The turn is told the task is archived, that a question-only turn leaves it Done, that it has no worktree for edits, and to run `task repository renew` before any Git change; its completed outcome leaves the task Done with no new worktree, the follow-up and its reply persist in the history across fresh reads, and switching the Done task's provider is still rejected.

`task repository renew` starts follow-up Git work after a pull request merged. It is rejected while the repository has no linked pull request, while the linked pull request is unmerged, and while the merged worktree has uncommitted changes, leaving the task unchanged. A merged PR status read persists that it merged, and the next turn is told the merged branch is finished and to renew before Git changes. Renewing from inside the agent's turn retires the record with its merged PR to the task's past repositories, keeps the merged branch, removes the old worktree once that turn ends, and creates a fresh worktree on a new suffixed branch based on the merge target as just fetched from the remote, so it holds the merged commits even when the local target is stale. A new pull request then opens from the fresh worktree, and the card shows the merged PR in purple beside the new one; once the task is Done, the archive row lists both. A Done task renews too, from inside its follow-up turn: it returns to In Progress with a fresh worktree for every repository whose worktree was removed (a past link only for records that had a pull request), and that turn's completed outcome moves it to Review, keeping both merged PRs on fresh reads.
The one-time lifecycle rollout clears task records and clean managed worktrees, preserves branches, and retains dirty managed worktrees with a notice.

With both pairs populated, the board keeps Blocked above Backlog and Waiting Response above In Progress, washes only the Waiting Response column in its purple tint (its pixels read purple where the other columns read neutral), allows vertical scrolling to reach lower backlog tasks, leaves Review as its own column, hides empty status sections, removes Done from the columns, and rejects manual changes to Codex-owned task status; ⌘F reveals and focuses a prominent board search that filters task cards by title as text changes, while close restores all cards. Answering a question without an explicit completed outcome leaves the task in Waiting Response. Task card titles use slightly expanded letter spacing and line spacing. The board's columns stay centered and clickable where they draw after a sideways scroll followed by a new card, without needing a window resize. Each board column is built from plugin atoms: the empty In Progress and Review columns show their empty state while the populated Backlog does not, and the Backlog's Add button opens a new task conversation.

A task in Waiting Response moves to Review through the CLI and on the board, both from its card's Move to Review context-menu item, which only Waiting Response cards offer, and by dragging the card onto the Review column. The move runs the same review gate as a completed outcome: local changes on a PR-linked worktree are committed before the task reaches Review. It clears the waiting status, persists across a fresh CLI/XPC read, keeps the linked pull request, returns a task already in Review unchanged, and the moved task can still complete to Done. A Backlog task is rejected and keeps its status; a task whose turn is still running while it shows Waiting Response is rejected and keeps both its status and its uncommitted changes; and when the pull request sync fails, the move reports the error, shown on the board as an alert, and leaves the task in Waiting Response; once GitHub reports the pull request merged, a retry commits local work, skips syncing the merged branch even though its remote is unreachable, and moves the task to Review.

The CLI publishes standard and custom progress only during an active task turn, persists each report across fresh CLI/XPC connections, rejects invalid reports, and clears explicitly. During an active turn the CLI accepts completed, in-progress, and waiting-response outcomes, rejects invalid or inactive outcomes, and persists the selected status; provider processes started from the CLI/XPC service or the app's composer inherit that app's bridge service name and store directory, and an outcome reported with exactly that inherited environment reaches the task. A successful turn without an outcome receives up to five private status nudges that each offer in-progress alongside completed and waiting-response; a completed report during a nudge moves the task to Review, a waiting-response report during a nudge stops the loop and leaves the task in Waiting Response, and no report after every nudge marks the task Blocked rather than Waiting Response, since the user was never asked anything. The board shows progress details and places completed tasks in Review and waiting outcomes in Waiting Response. New threads receive hidden progress and outcome instructions at thread start, and existing threads receive them on resume; turn requests do not repeat the instructions. Those instructions require updates at phase changes, around substantial tools, and at least every 30 seconds during long work. They place the outcome call, still the final CLI action, before the user-visible final reply, which ends the turn so it never ends on a tool call, and they tell the agent not to repeat an answer after a no-visible-output notice. Only an explicit completed outcome reaches Review. When a final answer ends with the outcome command written as text instead of run, the final answer, fresh history, and transcript hide that command, and it counts as the turn's outcome only when it names this task. A status nudge Playhouse sent shows its prompt and the agent's reply in Codex history and the visible transcript, including after later ordinary turns. Fresh Codex history after those nudges also retains the latest ordinary-turn diff while showing the nudge replies.

An in-progress outcome is accepted during an active turn, leaves the task In Progress, and makes Playhouse send a private continuation turn that names the in-progress report; a completed report during that continuation stops the loop at Review. When every turn reports in-progress, Playhouse sends exactly five continuation turns, keeps the task In Progress throughout, and then marks it Blocked with a continuation-limit reason instead of Waiting Response, since the user was never asked anything. Continuation prompts and replies appear in the conversation history as Playhouse-sent messages and their replies. The user taking the work back ends Playhouse's private driving: stopping a continuation keeps the Stop's Waiting Response with no failure reason, and a queued follow-up runs next instead of being buried under further continuations.

Progress reports clear when turns fail or are interrupted and when Codex requests user input; a staged completed outcome is discarded if its turn fails, leaving the task Blocked. The task card removes the report while lifecycle states remain Blocked or In Progress. A blocking structured question appears inline and moves the task to Waiting Response; its answer resumes the active turn in In Progress, and the answered turn finishes in Waiting Response. First-thread instructions distinguish source repository paths from active task worktree paths, allow read-only inspection without attaching a repo, and reserve repository add APIs for changes that need a worktree.
A rename waits for the real per-task operation lock, then persists across fresh CLI/XPC reads; rejecting a blank rename preserves the last valid title.

The conversation title's copy button places the task's exact persisted title on the pasteboard, including spaces, an ampersand and non-ASCII text, after a rename; the button confirms the copy with a checkmark and its 'Title copied' label, and fresh CLI/XPC reads report the same title the copy produced.

Root editing preserves order, removes duplicates, rejects an empty list, and waits for an active conversation turn; a stale Git-folder validation is rejected after a newer folder edit, and the newer roots remain saved.

Repository suggestions can be filtered and navigated with Up/Down, and Enter selects the highlighted repository; UI selection waits for an active turn and persists a pending auto branch. While the conversation is empty, a prominent theme-colored heading names all selected repositories and updates as repository APIs add or replace context; compact repository labels remain in the header without a duplicate repository summary. Dark and light themes use distinct prominent title colors, the supporting model prompt sits below with generous spacing, and the generic Start a conversation heading is absent. Additional context folders remain identifiable. The task repository API remains available during an active turn, prepares a managed worktree inside the app data directory's task-worktrees folder, updates saved repository selection, replaces repository context safely, and the paired UI shows API additions/removals. The main assistant is instructed to list repositories through Playhouse, inspect listed source paths read-only without attaching them, and add repositories only when it needs a task worktree for changes or commits.

Each repository row in the header's Add repository picker adds the repository alongside the selected ones when the row or its plus button is clicked, and its Replace button removes every selected repository and attaches only that one; the task repository API reaches the same add and replace results, duplicates are rejected, and the saved repository selection follows.

Pending repository branch, merge-from, and merge-to settings wait for an active conversation turn, then persist across fresh CLI/XPC reads; invalid settings leave prior values intact, and settings are locked after worktree creation. Each setting is edited in place: the pencil beside a value opens an inline field with a checkmark that saves only that field and keeps the editor open on the saved value, and clicking outside the field or pressing Escape dismisses the edit without saving. The settings popover is wider than before with a larger title, and the repository chip's remove button is a larger target.

A branch-from that exists only on a Git remote and was never fetched is fetched when repository settings are saved, and the pending record stores its remote-tracking branch; a branch-from missing locally and on every remote is rejected without changing the saved settings; a remote that can't be reached reports the fetch failure instead of a missing branch and also keeps the saved settings; starting the task fetches the remote branch again, so its worktree starts from the remote's latest commit even after the remote branch moved ahead, without making the remote branch the task branch's upstream.

With no branch-from given, a repository without an origin remote keeps its local default branch, while a repository whose origin has the default branch stores origin's remote-tracking branch as the pending branch-from. Starting the task fetches origin first, so the worktree starts from origin's latest commit even when the local default branch and its remote-tracking ref are stale and the local branch holds unpushed commits, without making the remote branch the task branch's upstream. When origin can't be reached at start, the task still starts from the last fetched origin commit.
If a pending repository is removed while its settings are being validated, the stale edit is rejected and the newer repository removal and context root remain saved.

Removing one of two pending repositories leaves the remaining repository in task context and remembered settings, while preserving the removed source repository; the next task restores only the remaining remembered repository. Removing a pending repository preserves other context folders; removing a clean managed worktree through the GUI waits for an active turn, while the task repository API removes it from context immediately and defers clean worktree deletion until the turn releases; a bridge service restart preserves the cleanup intent and a fresh request completes removal; if the active turn writes files before release, deferred cleanup preserves that worktree and its changes; a dirty worktree rejects removal and preserves its task record and files.

The task context menu offers deletion. Pending repository tasks delete without confirmation and preserve the source repository; confirmed deletion waits for an active conversation turn; clean started worktrees can be deleted; dirty started worktrees require confirmation, and canceling preserves the task and worktree. CLI delete-check derives and reports the confirmation requirement from saved task and worktree state without resuming the Codex thread; confirmed deletion removes the managed worktree. Deleting a task also removes its per-task preferences and any left by already-deleted tasks, while another task's preferences remain.

A real worktree-removal failure records the task title and task, thread, process, phase, and underlying error details, including bounded NSError user-info keys and values, without recording conversation text; the failed task and worktree remain available and deletion succeeds after the repository is restored.

The default parent can be read, changed, cleared, and an unavailable path is rejected; a fresh CLI read and repository discovery use the persisted parent. Dark and Light appearance choices persist, the removed PR conflict preference is absent from CLI/XPC and Settings, and appearance changes update the open Settings picker. Clearing the default parent does not change roots already saved on a task.

The configured-root workspace repos list API returns top-level Git repositories while excluding nested repositories and symlink targets. The conversation picker shows those suggestions, filters by repository name or parent path, and reports no matches for non-repository folders.

The CLI reads and writes ordered last-selected repositories across fresh XPC connections; repository batches prepare managed worktrees in order, use task-title-derived branches and main/main merge settings, and set the active task roots to those worktrees. The selected source repository list remains saved and applies to subsequent tasks. Invalid repository paths are rejected without changing the saved preference. In the UI, a new conversation automatically attaches saved repositories in order while the picker stays closed and the composer remains focused. Opening the picker and choosing another suggestion adds it to the ordered context and saved selection for subsequent conversations. Each saved selection also feeds a newest-first recent repository history of up to twenty repositories that keeps repositories after they are removed from the selection; the task repository recent command lists those that still exist and are not attached to the task, and rejects an unknown task. In the UI, attached repositories appear as large chips carrying a remove badge and the header shows no suggestion chips; removing a repository through its badge makes the add-repository picker list it under Recent before anything is typed, clicking it adds it back to the task and saved selection, and typing a query replaces the recent list with the regular search suggestions.

Applying an ordered repository batch with a valid repository followed by an empty Git repository fails without mutation: the CLI reports invalid_argument and fresh reads show no repository attachments or workspace roots; New Task automatically applies saved repositories; an invalid batch shows an error, attaches neither repository, keeps roots empty, preserves the saved order, and leaves the picker closed by default.

The CLI creates an Untitled task with no roots, logs task.create.succeeded for its ID, verifies empty history, and deletes it cleanly. New Task logs start and completion events with the same attempt ID and created task ID, then opens one empty conversation with the repository picker closed, the composer focused, and no create sheet. With no selected repositories, the empty conversation prominently says no repository is selected; typing starts immediately and, with a configured repository root, the UI enables standalone Send. Adding folder-only context leaves history empty, and backing out deletes the pending task without confirmation.

A real directory at the task-store write-lock path makes CLI task creation fail with operation_failed and leaves no task persisted; the paired New Task button shows the save error and writes correlated start and failure diagnostics with the same attempt ID, error domain, and code.

Creating a repository task leaves its selected branch pending while the composer automatically saves an unsent prompt as it is typed; clearing the composer clears the stored draft, backing out needs no Save button, and reopening restores the draft without creating a branch or worktree. Blank drafts cannot be stored, and invalid status changes are rejected without mutation. If the title is renamed while delayed title generation is in flight, the late result is skipped, the renamed title persists, and diagnostics record the skip reason without prompt or title text. A prompt saved through the CLI without submitting is an unsent draft, so the composer shows it when the task is reopened. A send that fails before any turn starts, such as one into a folder that no longer exists, returns its prompt to the composer as the draft, clears the pending marker and leaves the task out of In Progress.

Composer text typed while the agent responds is autosaved as an unsent draft together with its attached image, without ending the turn's submitted prompt or changing its status, and malformed draft images fail validation without changing the draft. A follow-up queued from elsewhere and dispatched after the turn does not replace the draft, which stays saved after the turn ends and is restored to the composer with its image after navigating away and after an app restart. Text steered or queued from the composer leaves the saved draft and does not reappear after the turn, and sending the draft clears it, its images leaving once the turn starts. A submitted prompt whose turn never started returns to the composer with its images, together with the draft typed after it.

Shift+Enter inserts a newline at the caret without sending and Return submits; multiline drafts persist, expand to the editor limit, remain scrollable and editable across reopening, and submitted prompts persist in history. As content is typed in short increments through successive wrapped lines after a line break, the newest insertion remains inside the visible composer viewport while its internal document follows the caret without scrolling backward. Typed straight quotes, apostrophes, and double hyphens stay literal rather than being substituted. Blank drafts cannot be sent or stored. Sending requires a configured repository root, while a task with no selected repository can still be sent as standalone. If a submitted prompt has no Codex thread or active send reservation after restart, the task returns to Waiting Response, clears its pending marker, preserves the draft, and returns it to the composer. Sending to an Untitled auto-branch task derives its branch from the generated title or prompt fallback before preparing the worktree and starting the conversation; if it is concurrently renamed while title generation is pending, the custom title determines the auto branch. A standalone Untitled task starts and persists its provider thread while background title generation is still pending. Pause remains disabled until the turn is interruptible. Diagnostics correlate title generation with the task and thread while excluding prompt and title text. Queued follow-ups persist with task and thread identity, dispatch after a completed turn, and remain visible for explicit retry after interruption. During an active turn, Return queues a follow-up and queued rows offer Steer. The obsolete footer Queue and Steer buttons are absent.

Selecting text in assistant and user messages shows a floating Add comment hint above and horizontally centered on the selected lines, including wrapped multiline selections; clicking it opens a compact inline comment field positioned beside the hint, with a clearly visible dark arrow on its light submit control. Added ranges render orange and persist after reopening. The composer shows the pending comment count. Structurally recognized comment context is hidden while similar ordinary text remains visible; comments are sent in insertion order with source ranges alongside ordinary composer text. Multiple comments can be added before one send, comment-only sends are enabled, and cancelling the compact field leaves none to submit. Pending comments take precedence over Goal-entry mode: submission sends them to the conversation, exits Goal-entry mode, and does not store the comment payload as a Goal objective. The agent is instructed to start each comment response line with the provider-neutral indexed protocol marker; the transcript renders that marker as a numbered prefix (1., 2.) whose hover opens a medium-sized hint with highlighted text and the user's comment, truncating long values while keeping them identifiable. The serialized payload and ordered response survive CLI/XPC history reload. Legacy Codex markers, response-annotations payloads, and annotation fields still restore their reply details. Consecutive paragraphs, headings, and list items of a reply form one selectable text: the comment reply's lines share one text with a paragraph each, and selecting across them adds one comment that highlights every covered paragraph, records the block it ends in alongside its start block and offsets (a comment inside one block keeps the original source fields), and is restored after reopening the conversation; the cross-block source survives CLI/XPC history reload. User messages render in a neutral gray, input-style bubble with a thin light border and light text rather than the blue accent fill.

A Claude turn that fails after Claude Code created its session leaves that session in place, and the next turn resumes it instead of claiming the same session ID again. After a Claude turn and Playhouse restart, if Claude cannot find its native resumed session, the retried fresh session receives the prior visible conversation from Playhouse's persisted transcript together with the new prompt. Claude completes the turn, and fresh CLI/XPC history and the visible UI retain both turns. A normal Claude resume continues using the native session without receiving duplicate handoff context.

An Untitled Claude task with a pending auto repository branch uses its selected provider to generate the title before worktree creation; the branch and title persist across fresh CLI/XPC reads and the visible task. If Claude title generation returns no title, the prompt becomes the title and branch fallback, and the conversation still starts in that worktree. A fresh `task title` request reproduces the generated title and provider (null when generation yields nothing), and `task reconcile` returns the settled task unchanged.

Claude turns for different conversations run at the same time instead of queueing on a shared turn slot. While one task's turn is held active, a second task's send starts in its own Claude process, runs its own tool, and completes with its own user and assistant messages before the held turn is released. Each turn's process uses its own task working directory, each conversation keeps only its own activity rows and measured durations, diagnostics record no queued-slot event and no prompt text, and the second conversation's answer is available while the first turn is still running.

A failing Claude turn does not disturb a conversation running in parallel. While one task's turn is held and then fails, a second task's send from a separate process completes on its own session and reaches Waiting Response; the failing task keeps its user message in its conversation, where the open and reopened task show it, with an empty composer and no unsent draft, records no final answer, and its provider process exit is the only failure in diagnostics. The UI shows the parallel answer after reopening its task with fresh history. While the failing task's conversation is open and its turn held, the parallel turn starts, finishes and advances only its own revision: CLI/XPC runtime still reports the held session active and interruptible and the parallel session inactive, and the open conversation still offers an enabled Stop and never shows the parallel answer.

Stopping one Claude turn pauses only that conversation while a second Claude conversation runs in parallel. The parallel conversation answers and keeps its own activity rows and measured durations while the first turn is still thinking; the stopped task moves to Waiting Response with no failure reason, records no answer, and leaves the parallel task's Waiting Response result untouched. A fresh CLI/XPC read confirms both results.

Two concurrent sends for the same task are serialized across the app and CLI/XPC paths against the local Codex app-server fixture; the second waits for the first, both complete on the persisted thread, the task remains In Progress while a send is active, and successful turns without outcome calls finish in Waiting Response.

When a steer misses its active turn, CLI/XPC and UI accept it into the durable queue for its own turn; opening an empty task waits for the model-aware prompt and omits the generic Start a conversation heading; with no active turn, a missed queued-row steer dispatches synchronously as its own turn and leaves the queue; queued fallback survives process exit or app relaunch and is drained exactly once; a missed regular or queued-row steer arriving during targeted queue dispatch is drained afterward exactly once; a follow-up being delivered stays claimed as dispatching and leaves the visible queue while its own turn runs; a missed queued-row steer from the CLI returns to the waiting queue and shows its row again in the app before the targeted turn ends; a failed targeted turn remains needs-action and does not drain later messages; malformed steer images fail validation; CLI/XPC steering routes image data to a UI-owned active turn and appears in the conversation. Command-Return steers the active turn with attached text and images, then clears the accepted draft and image preview; if the active turn changes before delivery, it clears the draft and queues the complete message for its own turn. Plain Return queues a follow-up with its attached image, clears the preview, and marks the row with its image count; the queued image persists across reopening without returning to the composer, and malformed queued images fail validation. Its row Steer uses the active turn ID, delivers both text and image to the provider, appears in the transcript with its image, and removes the item only after acceptance. The obsolete footer Queue and Steer buttons are absent and the active response control is labeled Stop response. Follow-ups persist across reopening, expose per-row Steer, delete, and more actions, and a distinct after-turn follow-up dispatches once after a matching completion and is removed only after successful delivery; removing an unknown queue ID fails without changing the queue.

Backlog draft images persist through fresh CLI/XPC reads and reopening the conversation, with the preview restored; saving more than 8 draft images fails with invalid_argument and preserves the existing attachment. The conversation composer also accepts pasted images, compresses large clipboard images to fit the 10 MB payload limit, sends PNG and JPEG data URLs through CLI/XPC and to Codex using the tagged image URL payload, reads Codex history image URLs, and keeps earlier images visible after a later text turn and history refresh. The provider-neutral conversation present-image API is included in agent instructions, validates and persists agent-produced PNG and JPEG files as assistant messages, and reopening the conversation renders each image visibly. Diagnostics record image MIME and encoded size without storing image payloads. Clicking a composer attachment, a user transcript attachment, or an agent-published assistant image opens the original image in a large viewer, which can be closed to return to the conversation; a published assistant image preserves the original file bytes.
Malformed image data is rejected with a visible composer error and an invalid_argument bridge response, without creating conversation history or advancing task status.

While a Claude Code turn is active in the app process, the agent's CLI/XPC image publication joins that active Claude transcript turn; after the provider finishes, history places the image before the later assistant answer, and reopening the conversation renders the exact published image. This active-turn attribution is Claude-specific: Codex history is composed from ordered timeline entries, so published images are standalone assistant messages verified for persistence and rendering in test_conversation_sends_image_attachments.

A Claude Code agent that has answered initialize and gone idle receives a user message carrying a screenshot larger than its input FIFO's buffer: the send completes with Claude's answer, the agent receives the whole image, the user message keeps that image when history is read over a fresh CLI/XPC connection and when the conversation is reopened, and a later text turn in the same conversation still completes. Claude Code's runtime, like the kqueue-reading fixture, is never woken by one oversized blocking write, so such a message must reach it without freezing the daemon. Codex agents talk over a socket and are not affected.

While a Codex turn is active, CLI/XPC image publication avoids requesting provider history; the assistant image is tied to that turn, appears after its native response and before the next turn in ordered history, and remains visible after reopening the conversation.

While a Claude Code fixture turn started by another caller is still running, its commentary and tool activity raise the task's conversation revision in the daemon's runtime snapshot, a held turn with no visible output yet leaves that revision unchanged, and mid-turn history, read from Playhouse's own Claude transcript, already returns the prompt, the commentary, and the in-progress tool activity before any final answer. A conversation reopened after its send, and so no longer reading that turn's stream, shows the commentary and the running tool row while the turn is still held, then the final answer once it settles; the revision rises again when the turn ends.

While a Codex app-server fixture turn started by another caller is still running, its commentary and tool activity raise the task's conversation revision in the daemon's runtime snapshot, a held turn with no visible output yet leaves that revision unchanged, and mid-turn history, read from Codex's native thread while the turn holds, already returns the prompt, the commentary, and the in-progress tool activity before any final answer. A conversation reopened after its send, and so no longer reading that turn's stream, shows the commentary and the running tool row while the turn is still held, then the final answer once it settles; the revision rises again when the turn ends. With a non-default model selected, those mid-turn history reads use the thread the running turn already loaded and never send thread/resume with history's default model.

While a Claude Code fixture reply streams in held stages below its question, mid-turn CLI/XPC history holds every streamed line before the newest, which Claude may still extend as its answer, once each and in order after the question, with no final line until the reply is released, and the settled turn ends with its final line after every streamed line. In the visible transcript, a reader at the bottom follows the reply: once it outgrows the viewport, the newest streamed line stays in view and the question scrolls away. Scrolling up stops following, so the next stage leaves the reader's position unchanged and its lines out of view; scrolling back to the bottom resumes following, so the next stage's newest line is in view while the turn is still running, and the settled turn leaves its final line in view. A short follow-up with a tool call then becomes the newest turn, and the newest history page ends with its question, tool call, and answer after the streamed turn. Scrolled as far down as it goes, the transcript has no blank overscroll: while the held reply outgrows the viewport it ends at its newest line, and the settled reply, whose streamed lines fold into Worked for, and the short follow-up, both once it settles and after the settled conversation is reopened, keep the newest question pinned near the top. Following is shared transcript presentation, so one representative provider covers it.

A Claude Code fixture turn that writes commentary, runs shell commands (one failing) and an MCP call, then answers keeps each call in Playhouse's own transcript placed after the message written before it. Once a later turn starts, CLI/XPC history still returns the earlier turn's calls as timeline activities, apart from the latest turn's activities: each shell call carries its stated purpose, its exact command and the output it returned, the failing call reports failed, and the MCP call exposes neither its arguments nor its raw result. A history page returns only the calls placed on its own messages, so the newest page carries none of them and the page before it carries them all. While its turn is the latest, a call stays in Worked for and is not shown inline. Once a later turn starts, the visible conversation shows each earlier call inline between those messages, in order, as a row with the tool's name, its purpose, and IN and OUT blocks clipped until expanded; the MCP row has no IN or OUT block, the turn's answer renders a numbered list written right under a paragraph line as separate items whose inline code text is unchanged, and the rows are still there after reopening the task.

A Codex app-server fixture thread whose earlier turn reports commentary, command executions (one failing) and an MCP call between its messages keeps those items in their place in history: once a later turn starts, CLI/XPC history returns each earlier call as a timeline activity placed after the message the thread listed before it, with its working directory, exact command and aggregated output, the failing command reports failed, and the MCP call exposes neither its arguments nor its raw result. Commentary on either side of a call stays a separate message instead of merging across it. A history page returns only the calls placed on its own messages, so the newest page carries none of them and the page before it carries them all. While its turn is the latest, a call stays in Worked for and is not shown inline. Once a later turn starts, the visible conversation shows each earlier call inline between those messages, in order, as a row with the tool's name, its working directory, and IN and OUT blocks clipped until expanded; the MCP row has no IN or OUT block, the turn's answer renders a numbered list written right under a paragraph line as separate items whose inline code text is unchanged, and the rows are still there after reopening the task.

MCP and dynamic tool lifecycle updates coalesce by stable item ID into distinct visible conversation rows; each call reports its start and measured duration, and completed durations persist through history reload. While a tool call holds the sent turn active, the transcript never shows blank space: the submitted user message is in view, or, once the turn's activity has outgrown the viewport and the transcript follows it, the message sits above the latest live activity, which is in view. The latest active process, including a long command, appears outside Working for on one truncated line; older active processes remain inside, and completion moves it inside. The conversation header has no live activity line while responding. Working for renders open while the turn runs, so its progress is visible without a click, and it is still open after leaving and reopening the task mid-turn; every in-flight call is readable from mid-turn history. A collapse the reader performs mid-turn is honored and survives the activity updates that follow, and the final answer closes the section back into a clean collapsed Worked for. The expanded Working for list shows each call's live or completed duration. In-progress, completed, and failed statuses, server/tool identity, and safe result summaries render without duplicate rows, including when later-turn items follow the calls in history. Arguments and raw result text are never exposed.

contextCompaction item/started and item/completed coalesce into one concise timeline event; missing summaries ignore malformed opaque payload fields and never render their data, and the event survives thread history reload with correct prompt/response ordering.

Reopening a 120-message conversation immediately presents only the latest user question, pinned to the top of the viewport with its answer below. Scrolling upward loads earlier messages automatically in 40-message batches, including when the latest turn alone is shorter than the viewport, while keeping the anchored message in place and preserving chronological order. No separate control is needed on systems that report scroll position; below macOS 15 the transcript keeps an explicit Load earlier messages control inside that runway instead. A conversation that was empty when it opened establishes no window and keeps the newest 40 messages rendered as they arrive. Reloading history in place reopens on that same latest turn and keeps upward paging working. CLI/XPC history remains complete and ordered across fresh reads and across an in-place provider switch, and a paged read returns only the newest 80 messages with the count of the 40 before them, while paging backward returns those earlier messages in order. The transcript's runway above the rendered window is as tall as the unrendered history is estimated to be, from the loaded messages and the stored count a paged read reports, so the scroller knob already reflects the whole conversation when the latest turn opens and keeps about its size as older batches are revealed; one long upward scroll deep into that runway reveals every batch it passes, reading the stored page as needed, and lands on the first messages.

A sent prompt followed by a 120-message turn, so that it lies outside the newest history page, never returns to the composer when the task is reopened: the composer is empty, the task keeps hasUnsentDraft false and its last sent prompt as the saved prompt, and the CLI newest page of 80 messages leaves out the earlier messages. Only the saved draft flag decides draft restoration, so the same task restores a real unsent draft after it is typed.

Claude turns are stored row by row in the SQLite conversation store: a user image is kept out of the message text payload, and recording a later turn writes only that turn's own rows without rewriting earlier turns. CLI/XPC history stays complete by default; with --limit it reads only the stored turns covering the newest messages and returns those messages plus the count of earlier ones, and --before pages backward to the first message, with pages that join into the complete ordered history, carry its activities, and fill in the image only on the page that holds its message; this still holds after another turn completes. A non-positive or non-numeric limit fails with invalid_argument, an unknown --before message fails with not_found, and an empty conversation returns an empty page. Reopening the conversation in the visible UI reads only the newest page and pins the latest turn, scrolling straight down from that pin keeps the latest question near the top and the latest answer below it with no blank overscroll, and scrolling up then reads the older page from the store as the reader scrolls up until the first turn and its image are shown, and a turn sent afterwards from the composer keeps the earlier pages loaded without reading them again.

During a parent turn, Working for renders open and active agents appear as individual named rows, each with an arrow that opens it, outside it, with available path/model/reasoning metadata and started-working wording; a mid-turn collapse the reader performs is honored. When the final answer arrives, all agent rows collapse inside Worked for alongside other Codex activity; expanding it reveals clickable agent rows. The UI fixture pauses after the final answer to verify this before turn completion while Stop response remains available. Completed, interrupted, and unknown states survive history reload and remain inspectable after reopening. The child thread opens as read-only through thread/read, thread/turns/list, and thread/items/list without editable controls or thread/resume, and diagnostics retain safe RPC outcomes while excluding conversation text, command output, and diffs. Multiple Codex message deltas and command-output deltas are summarized per item with counts and byte totals, flushed at turn completion, and excluded from individual notification records; lifecycle notifications remain individually logged, and diagnostics exclude conversation text, command output, and diffs. A fresh `conversation subagent-history` read returns the completed child's stored conversation content.

Selecting Plan mode keeps planning active across completed turns and reopening; follow-up instructions start another plan turn, and Start Implementing is hidden until a first message is sent and while the agent waits on answers to its questions, then stays enabled with an empty composer, switches to Code mode, and starts an implementation turn; subsequent composer messages remain Code turns. The plan renders automatically as Markdown with visible spacing, remains selectable and copyable as one complete text view, and CLI events and bridge history preserve the exact plan text and latest implementation handoff. Ordered list items stay on separate lines instead of being merged, including a list that starts on the line right after a paragraph without a blank line, and a fenced code block renders as a distinct block with its declared language label and a copy action that places its exact source on the pasteboard. A Markdown pipe table renders as a distinct bordered grid with a header row and data rows instead of raw pipe/dash text, preserving cell content and column alignment and wrapping a long cell onto every line it needs instead of cutting it off with an ellipsis, while CLI/XPC history preserves the exact raw table source text. Multiple plan deltas are summarized per item with count and byte totals at turn completion, with no per-delta notification records and no plan text in diagnostics. While the first plan is still streaming in and fits the viewport, the question that started it stays pinned near the top of the transcript, consistent with the user message preceding its final answer in CLI/XPC history. The plan streams in four held deltas that end inside a paragraph, inside a list item after it, and inside the fenced code block; CLI/XPC events carry exactly those deltas in order, and at each held stage the plan's one prose text view and its code block show exactly the text streamed so far, with nothing repeated or left over from an earlier stage, before the completed plan shows its whole code block.

A task with neither a repository nor a working folder can still plan, but once the plan exists its Start Implementing button is disabled and explains why: its tooltip and accessibility value read "Add a repository to this task to start implementing.", and a visible No repository warning beside it carries the same reason and opens the repository picker. Bridge state for the planned task has no workspace roots and no repository worktrees. Adding a repository gives the task a workspace root; in the still-open conversation the warning disappears and Start Implementing enables without reopening the task, then switches to Code mode and starts an implementation turn recorded after the plan turn, which runs in the task's created repository worktree as its only workspace root.

The composer keeps the committed model and effort stable while the picker is open, then updates when it is dismissed. Its popover lists provider models and includes an accessible discrete effort slider with Low, Medium, High, and Extra High choices, constrained by model-reported effort support when available; the visible opaque white knob has no focus border, the 6-point track is visibly thick, and the slider responds to dragging and keyboard arrows. The selected model is global across conversations for the active provider, persists through fresh CLI/XPC reads and reopening, and remains isolated between providers; a saved per-conversation model migrates into the global preference on first read; effort persists per conversation. Malformed model IDs and unsupported efforts are rejected without replacing prior choices. The UI opens a second conversation and shows the global model selection; unsupported modes and malformed model IDs are rejected before creating history.

CLI/XPC Goal set/get/pause/resume/clear persist the objective and lifecycle state across fresh connections and enable the Goals app-server feature; setting the same active Goal preserves its timer generation, clearing then setting another Goal creates a new generation with a fresh baseline, setting a Goal moves the task to In Progress, and invalid blank objectives preserve the current Goal. The UI restores saved Goals; the opt-in live Codex integration confirms native startup, verifies the first Goal retains its elapsed duration, restores a legacy completion without timing metadata, and confirms a second Goal timer begins near zero; renders each achieved summary as a conversation item that visibly moves with scrolling and is anchored to its completing turn, verifies a later user follow-up appears after the prior achievement through turn completion, and preserves both items and their ordering in the read-only Done archive. Native turn activation is owned by the retained GUI runtime.

A window and the CLI use one Codex app-server per Codex home. Every Codex request against one data folder (sends on two tasks, Goal set/get/pause/clear, history and usage refreshes, from the CLI and, in the UI, from an open window as well) runs on the same recorded server process, which listens on the shared unix socket with features.goals=true and the caller's CODEX_HOME and is the one live Codex manifest; it keeps running after every CLI Goal call, including a rejected blank objective, and a CLI call that spells the same CODEX_HOME differently reuses it. A send on the second task while the first task's Goal is active leaves that Goal active. The work turn Codex runs for the Goal is active and interruptible whether the window or the CLI set it; a history read during it, even with another model selected, never resumes the thread, and once pausing the Goal ends the turn, history resumes the thread with the selected model. A usage read the server never answers times out without stopping the server and keeps the last known Codex account, and the next refresh reads it again. In the UI, the window sets a Goal and follows the turn Codex starts for it, which stays active and interruptible while the CLI sends on the second task and ends when the window pauses the Goal; a Goal the CLI sets appears in the open window without reopening the task, the window's pause and clear reach the CLI's Goal reads, and the Agents info block shows the Codex account read through that server.

A Codex app-server started under the earlier shared-client key, which also held two goal flags, is retired by the next daemon. When its daemon dies and a fresh daemon starts for the data folder, it reconnects to the legacy server only to retire it: with no turn left to follow, the server is stopped and its manifest removed, and the next Codex send, from the CLI or, in the UI, from the window, runs on one new server under the current key (executable, Codex home, data folder), leaving one live Codex server.
Claude AskUserQuestion requests with no questions are rejected through the control protocol, fail the turn, and mark the task Blocked; the UI shows the blocked task and its intervention indicator.

Claude's pending AskUserQuestion is persisted and restored from fresh CLI/XPC history after the provider turn ends; the task remains Waiting Response while unanswered, and answering resumes the saved Claude session in In Progress, delivers the answer, hides the private recovery prompt and redacts secret answers from Playhouse history, clears pending state, and returns to Waiting Response. While the recovery turn applying the answer runs, the answered question is no longer pending in history or shown in the reopened conversation, which still shows the question that started it, and the task is In Progress; if that recovery dies mid-turn, the question returns for retry with the task in Waiting Response, and answering again succeeds.

A Claude AskUserQuestion asked during a Plan mode turn persists its mode; after its provider process ends, answering resumes the saved Claude session in Plan mode rather than silently downgrading to Code mode, relaunching the recovery turn with --permission-mode plan.

A Claude background Agent/Task call renders a live subagent activity that stays in progress through its launch confirmation and intermediate progress, resolves only once its real completion notification arrives, and keeps the turn open until then instead of settling early. A status-only completion update is not shown as an agent result; the summary-bearing notification is persisted as one normal assistant message in the parent conversation, appears in the visible transcript as the agent's row (named, finished working, with an arrow) rather than a reply bubble, opens the report in the read-only agent window when clicked, and survives fresh CLI/XPC history reads and app reopening without duplication. A failed background agent remains inspectable as a failed activity, and its error summary is not added as an assistant result. When a background agent's notification wakes the parent after its result, the turn stays open through that resumed work, including when the last agent finishes while the woken parent is still streaming, and ends only with the parent's next result, keeping its final answer and both agent reports. A failed agent whose notification the running turn already consumed ends the send promptly instead of waiting for a wake. The system prompt Playhouse appends for Claude lets it run shell commands and agents in the foreground or background, forbids only processes detached with & or nohup, says it can end its response while background work runs instead of waiting and must report the outcome only after the background results, and no longer tells it to sleep, keep shell commands in the foreground, or keep its turn open for work it started.

A Claude Bash call launched with run_in_background stays an in-progress activity after its launch confirmation and keeps the turn open after Claude's result while the shell runs, and still after the shell's notification empties the background task list, until the parent turn Claude Code wakes to deliver that notification sends its own result. The woken turn's answer is the final answer, the outcome it reports moves the task to Review without private outcome reminders, and the shell's completion resolves its activity with the command status without becoming an agent report. When the shell finishes before Claude's first result, so the woken turn starts before that result arrives, the turn waits for both results.

A Claude turn answers while a background review runs, the review's notification arrives right after that answer, and the woken turn adds nothing and reports no outcome; the review's report and the answer both stay in history. Playhouse's private status nudge then starts a turn that keeps working, and a message the user steers into it is kept too: its commentary, its shell call, the background suite it launches, that suite's report delivered in a notification-driven woken turn, the screenshot it presents, and its final answer are streamed and recorded in order, and the completed outcome it reports moves the task to Review. Fresh history, a paged history read, and a later ordinary turn all keep that work, with the final report as the latest message before the later turn, while the nudge prompt Playhouse sent is shown once as its own message and no placeholder replaces it.

A Codex turn that reports no outcome receives Playhouse's private status nudge, and the nudged turn keeps working, with a message the user steers into it kept too: its commentary, its shell command, and its final answer are streamed and appear in fresh history after the earlier answer, with the shell command as a timeline tool row, and the completed outcome it reports moves the task to Review. The nudge prompt Playhouse sent is shown once as its own message and no placeholder replaces it, including after a later ordinary turn.

A Claude turn whose result is already out while a background shell keeps it open is still steerable: a queued follow-up's Steer reaches the running turn instead of silently staying queued, leaves the queue, appears in the conversation, and the turn waits for Claude's answer to it before the woken parent turn ends the send.

When Claude Code starts the provider turn that would deliver a finished background task's notification and then says nothing at all, Playhouse settles that turn on its own instead of leaving it open and the task In Progress forever: a follow-up queued while the turn was still parked stays queued through the silent wake, the send finishes and the task reaches Review, and that follow-up is then delivered in its own turn rather than stranded in the queue. A woken turn that is alive and merely slow to speak is not cut off by that backstop: it stays quiet past the grace a consumed notification gets and still ends the turn on its own answer.

If Claude fails while applying an answer after restart and echoes the answer or recovery instructions, Playhouse returns a generic error, preserves the pending question for retry while the task stays in Waiting Response, and keeps the prompt out of history, saved task state, and diagnostics.

Codex's pending structured question persists after its provider process exits and leaves the task in Waiting Response while unanswered; Playhouse restores it from fresh CLI/XPC history, keeps provider switching blocked, requires the user to re-enter the secret once, and applies the answers in one recovery turn. The live recovery stream retains safe assistant text while redacting secret echoes; persisted history hides secret recovery responses, provider activities, and file-change diffs. A later non-sensitive Codex turn keeps its own diff and safe response visible in refreshed CLI/UI history while the earlier secret stays absent. In one task, a no-secret recovery response remains visible after a later secret recovery while the secret response is hidden. Secret answers with surrounding whitespace are still redacted when Codex normalizes its echo; the visible UI shows the safe response immediately and after app restart. The first prompt, delivered before the provider exited although its send reported failure, is in history, never returns to the composer, and is not saved as an unsent draft.

When Codex recovery and a later thread-resume/history read error echo the full recovery prompt and answers, Playhouse preserves the pending question while the task stays in Waiting Response, uses a generic visible error, and redacts private content from returned history, saved task state, diagnostics, and error text across fresh CLI/XPC reads and app restarts.

Claude AskUserQuestion requests are delivered through the control path and move the task to Waiting Response while pending; the question's Markdown, header, and option descriptions reach the client, and the UI renders the question inline with its Markdown formatted at the reply text size, its header, and each option's description, preserves it across conversation switching, and sends a later answer to Claude before the turn ends in Waiting Response.

A successful Claude turn with an unanswered AskUserQuestion stays In Progress without outcome nudges; after the user answers, the next successful turn receives a hidden CLI status nudge. A question raised during that nudge is rejected through Claude's control protocol with completed, in-progress, and waiting-response instructions, which fails the private turn; both the question and the private rejection instructions stay out of the transcript. Playhouse then stops driving the work and marks the task Blocked naming that reason, rather than spending the remaining nudges.

MCP tool/requestUserInput structured questions raised in Plan mode remain in the conversation and move the task to Waiting Response while unanswered; leaving and reopening the conversation preserves the pending question, keyed answers resume the provider turn in In Progress, and the answered turn reports no outcome, so Playhouse drives a private status nudge; when that private turn cannot complete, the task settles in Blocked naming that reason instead of Waiting Response. A parallel conversation retains its own question and thread; the original conversation receives and answers a second question in its original Plan mode, and completing either conversation preserves the other pending request.

Non-blocking structured questions render inline, remain pending after switching to another conversation, and keep the task In Progress through fresh CLI/XPC history reconciliation after provider exit until answered. Free-text questions expose a selectable Other choice, select it when text is entered, keep it exclusive of listed answers, and deliver the free-text answer through CLI/XPC and visible UI. Answering resumes the provider turn without status nudges while its own pending question is still being resolved; the resumed turn returns to Waiting Response once the pending question clears, and the recovered secret answer stays redacted everywhere.

Async agentMessage questions retain choices and a free-text prompt in live updates and fresh CLI/XPC history, retain accepted-turn model attribution during an active history reload, stay separate from later assistant text, and receive validated answers through the shared manager during and after an active turn. The UI shows inline answer cards instead of raw bullet text, blocks incomplete answers, preserves answered cards across reopening, and displays both submitted answers and responses.

An async question answered after its turn ends stays Pending when the first follow-up fails, rejects duplicate answers across fresh CLI/XPC connections, and becomes Answered only after an explicit queued retry succeeds. The paired UI keeps the card and queue action visible across reopening and then displays the delivered response. A fresh `conversation answered-async` read lists no answered questions while the answer is pending and lists the question once it is delivered.

Turn start persists In Progress; a genuine interrupted outcome remains Blocked with its reason, while restart recovery returns stale In Progress work to Waiting Response with its prompt and conversation available. A saved prompt whose turn never started returns to Waiting Response with its draft intact and can be continued; a turn running when the window quits cleanly or is killed keeps running in the bridge daemon, stays In Progress with its prompt visible after relaunch, finishes, and allows a follow-up. Interrupted outcomes and diagnostics persist across connections; a new prompt can finish in Review. The live turn's activity section renders open and folds away when the interrupted turn settles without an answer, on the conversation that stayed open; the interrupted turn adds no final answer and keeps the activity it reported. A queued follow-up remains visible as needing action after interruption, survives reopening, and is dispatched only after an explicit retry; the completed retry becomes the task's latest saved prompt.

A failed turn preserves its blocked reason and appears in the compact Blocked section above Backlog with a user-intervention indication; retrying clears that section, and the successful retry returns to Waiting Response without an explicit completed outcome.

The task view lists every file changed from the task branch's recorded base in a Changes section below a collapsed Viewed section, including committed branch changes and current staged, unstaged, and untracked edits, and excluding commits unique to the base branch. Marking a file viewed saves its current contents, stages the file in Git, and adds a Viewed entry that keeps showing the reviewed work from the branch base to that snapshot. Work done after that review is listed again under Changes and diffed against the saved snapshot, so one file can appear in both sections at once; a path with no content in the branch base and no current file is zero net change and is hidden entirely, even with a stale viewed snapshot, rather than showing a ghost entry. Selecting text or JSON files opens a calculated side-by-side diff whose header names the baseline used. Viewed snapshots persist across fresh CLI/XPC connections. Files that aren't current Changes entries, including already-viewed and unknown paths, are rejected by the mark-viewed CLI operation, and the UI offers that action only for Changes entries. Uncommitted filenames are green. Opening one diff after another serves each file's own content from the side-by-side editor the app loads once per session, so a later diff reuses that warm editor instead of starting Monaco again. Diagnostics record inventory and file-read outcomes without logging file contents.

The Changes section header offers Mark all as viewed while it lists files: one action saves a viewed snapshot of every current Changes entry and stages each in Git, so Changes empties and every file is listed under Viewed, and the operation reports how many files it marked, zero when nothing is pending.
